text:
alessandra: Quick proposal — add a single "stream-anchor" header to edge requests so we can resume/hedge midstream without re-sending the full input.

mike: short version: how's this different from existing resume tokens?

alessandra: resume tokens are heavy (kv cache pointers + per-conn state). stream-anchor would be a lightweight opaque id that upstream can attach to a persistent in-memory cursor. goal: let gateway hedge or reroute to a warm upstream replica and request 'resume at anchor X'.

sam: sounds neat. open questions: ordering guarantees and de-duplication. if we resume, will upstream re-play already-delivered tokens?

alessandra: server-side contract: anchor points are always at safe boundaries (token boundaries or chunk boundaries). upstream must idempotently accept "resume: anchor" and reply with next bytes. if it cannot resume (evicted/ttl), it returns 410 + suggestion to fallback to cold-start.

jordan: what about client-visible semantics? user should not see duplicated tokens. maybe gateway tracks per-call last-delivered-offset and filters duplicates on resume.

mike: that sounds heavy. filtering at gateway means we need to reconstruct tokenized offsets for every resume.

alessandra: agreed. alternative: upstream guarantees not to resend past anchor. simpler but requires state retention on all replicas for X seconds.

sam: retention window becomes the SLA knob. can we make it configurable per-tenant? Dedicated customers may want longer windows.

jordan: also need observability hooks: metric for resume success/failure, and tracing for anchor issuance + resume attempts.

ops-bot: Deployment note: new header must be opt-in behind feature flag. Rollout plan: 1) gateway passes header but no-op upstream; 2) backend implements resume API; 3) enable routing hedges to resume-capable pool.

alessandra: example header sketch:

```
X-Stream-Anchor: 8f3b2a4c
X-Stream-Anchor-Version: v1
```

and resume request: `POST /resume` with anchor in body. Upstream responses:
- 200 streaming body (continuation)
- 410 anchor-not-found (suggest cold-start)
- 403 anchor-unauthorized (invalid tenant)

mike: compatibility: if gateway hedges to multiple upstreams, we must ensure hedged replica either supports resume or fallback path uses normal cold start. Could do capability flag in service discovery.

sam: cost model: warm-resume avoids re-tokenization & long kv-rebuild, reduces latency but increases memory footprint for anchor retention.

jordan: security: anchor must be bound to tenant and call idempotency key. Signed HMAC maybe?

alessandra: yep. plan: anchor = HMAC(tenant_id + call_id + nonce). upstream verifies HMAC and checks call_id namespace.

mike: concern: backpressure & stream windows. Resumes might create bursty tail-loads as queued resumes hit an upstream. Need admission control and a resume-rate-limit per-zone.

sam: also think about partial deliveries — if we resume from chunk boundaries we need to publish explicit trailer that says "anchor-ready: <id>" so gateway can mark safe points.

alessandra: good call. propose trailer format: `Anchor-Ready: 8f3b2a4c;offset=1234` emitted by upstream periodically and on flush.

jordan: tests: fuzzer for interleaved hedges + resume failures + lost-ack. Also chaos scenario where resume pool is evicted mid-replay.

ops-bot: @eng-runtime please add feature-flag and metric stubs into next sprint board.

alessandra: I'll draft a short RFC with compatibility matrix, retention defaults, and rollout checklist. assigning reviewers: @mike @sam @jordan

mike: +1, prefer conservative defaults (short retention, gating by tenant usage)

sam: +1, add perf microbench for resume vs cold-start

jordan: +1 — include tracing span design and alert thresholds for resume-fail rate

alessandra: thanks everyone — I'll post the RFC link here once ready.
